voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Portland, Oregon. November twenty-fourth, nineteen seventy-one. A man who called himself Dan Cooper boarded a flight to Seattle.
In the air, he passed a note. He said he had a bomb. He asked for two hundred thousand dollars, and four parachutes.
In Seattle, the passengers were released, and the money was delivered. The plane took off again, into the night.
Somewhere over southwest Washington, the rear stairs came down. When the plane landed in Reno, he was gone.
In nineteen eighty, a boy found some of the money on a bank of the Columbia River. The man has never been identified.
